check.title: Is your name on the voter list?
check.lead: You can vote only if your name is on the electoral roll (voter list) where you live. Having a voter ID card is not enough. Check before every election.

ways.title: With your voter ID number (EPIC)
ways.body: Your EPIC number is the 10-character number printed on your voter ID card. Choose **Search by EPIC**, type the number, pick your state, type the captcha, and press Search.

ways.title: With your details
ways.body: No card? Choose **Search by Details**. Enter your name, your father's, mother's or spouse's name, your age or date of birth, your gender, state, district and constituency. If nothing shows up, try other spellings.

ways.title: With your mobile number
ways.body: Choose **Search by Mobile**. This works only if your phone number is already linked to your voter record. Enter the number, the captcha, and the OTP you receive.

check.result: If you are on the list, you will see your name, your Assembly constituency, your part number, your serial number in that part, and your polling station. Take a screenshot. It helps on voting day.

other.title: ECINET app
other.body: ECINET is the official app of the Election Commission for Android and iPhone. It brings together voter search, forms, application tracking and the older Voter Helpline app. Website: [ecinet.eci.gov.in](https://ecinet.eci.gov.in/)

other.title: Call 1950
other.body: The voter helpline can check your name for you.

other.title: Ask your BLO
other.body: Every polling booth area has a Booth Level Officer (BLO) who keeps the voter list for that area. You can find your BLO and book a call with them on ECINET.

check.notFoundTitle: Not on the list? Don't panic
notFound: Search again with other spellings, or with fewer details, for example only your name and age.
Search at your old address. Your name may still be listed where you lived before.
Registered before but moved? Use **Form 8** to shift your address.
check.toMove: How to move your vote with Form 8

register.title: Get your name on the voter list
register.lead: Registering is free. You can apply online or on paper. If you have never been registered, you need **Form 6**.
register.cta: Apply on the ECI voter portal
who: You are a citizen of India.
You are 18 or older on 1 January, 1 April, 1 July or 1 October. If you are 17, you can apply early. Your name is added when you turn 18.
You ordinarily live at the address where you want to vote.
You are not registered anywhere else.
register.photo: A recent passport-size colour photo with a white background (4.5 cm × 3.5 cm). Eyes open, full face visible.
age: Class 10 or Class 12 certificate that shows your date of birth
address: Water, electricity or gas bill for that address (at least 1 year)
Current bank or post office passbook
Registered sale deed (if you own the house)
register.docsNote: The address proof can be in your name or in the name of your parent or spouse. If you have none of these, you can still apply. Write the name of another document, and an officer will visit to check your address. Aadhaar is asked for, but you can say that you do not have it.

steps.title: Open the voter portal
steps.body: Go to [voters.eci.gov.in](https://voters.eci.gov.in/) or open the ECINET app.

steps.title: Sign up with your mobile number
steps.body: Create an account with your mobile number and the OTP you receive.

steps.title: Choose Form 6
steps.body: Pick **Form 6**, the form for new voters.

steps.title: Fill in your details
steps.body: Your name, a relative's name, your date of birth and your address. Write your name in English and in your state's language to avoid spelling mistakes.

steps.title: Upload your photo and documents
steps.body: Upload your photo, age proof and address proof. Make sure the photos are clear and easy to read.

steps.title: Submit and save the reference number
steps.body: After you submit, write down the reference number or take a screenshot. You need it to track your application.

steps.title: A BLO may visit you
steps.body: The Booth Level Officer may come to your home to check your address. Keep your original documents ready.

steps.title: Track it and get your voter ID
steps.body: Track your application on the voter portal with your reference number. Once it is approved, you can download your e-EPIC (digital voter ID). The card is sent to you by Speed Post, free of cost.

register.offline: Fill in a paper Form 6 and hand it to your BLO, or to the office of the Electoral Registration Officer (ERO) for your area.
otherForms: **Form 8**: if you moved house, or to correct a mistake in your entry.
**Form 7**: to object to a wrong name on the list, or to remove a name.
register.timing: Your name must be on the voter list by the last date of nominations for an election. After that date the list is frozen. An application that is still pending does not count.
register.warning: Giving false information in these forms is a crime. It can lead to up to one year in jail, a fine, or both (Section 31, Representation of the People Act, 1950).

move.title: Moved to a new city? Move your vote too
move.lead: You can be registered in only one place: where you ordinarily live. If you have moved for work or study, you can shift your registration with **Form 8**. Your name is then removed from the list at your old address.
move.cta: Shift your address on the ECI voter portal
problem: Many people move to another city for work and rent a room or a flat. Their name stays on the voter list back home. On voting day they are far away. Going home costs money and days off work, so many of them do not vote.

The Election Commission of India says that not being able to vote because of migration within the country is one of the prominent reasons for low turnout. In the 2019 general election, turnout was 67.4%. More than 30 crore registered voters did not vote.

ECI says many migrants do not register where they work because they move house often, feel less connected to local issues, or do not want their name removed back home where they have family or property.

In 2022, ECI proposed a remote voting machine, so that migrants could vote for their home constituency from the city where they live. As of October 2026, we have not found any ECI announcement that it is being used in elections. Until it is, the practical choices are to move your registration, or to plan your trip home early.
shift: You have lived here for a while and plan to stay.
You cannot travel home on voting day.
You want a say in the place where you live and work.
stay: You go home often and can travel to vote.
Your home is where you ordinarily live, and you are only away for a short time.
move.decideNote: Either way, you cannot be on two lists at once. Check that your name is on the list where you choose to vote.
move.proofLead: You need one of these for your new address. It can be in your name, or in the name of your parent or spouse.
proof: Aadhaar card with your new address
Bank or post office passbook with your new address
Water, electricity or gas bill for that address (at least 1 year)
move.tipsTitle: Tips if your name is not on the rent papers
tips: Update the address in your bank account or Aadhaar first. Then use it as your proof.
Ask your landlord or PG owner for a registered rent agreement.
Students can register at their hostel address.
If you have none of these documents, write the name of another document in the form. An officer will visit to check that you live there.

steps.title: Find your current entry
steps.body: Search for your name on [electoralsearch.eci.gov.in](https://electoralsearch.eci.gov.in/) and note your EPIC number.

steps.title: Log in to the voter portal
steps.body: Go to [voters.eci.gov.in](https://voters.eci.gov.in/) or open the ECINET app, and log in with your mobile number.

steps.title: Choose Form 8, Shifting of residence
steps.body: Say whether you moved within the same constituency or to a different one.

steps.title: Enter your new address
steps.body: Type your full new address and upload one address proof.

steps.title: Submit and save the reference number
steps.body: A BLO may visit your new address to check that you live there.

steps.title: Get your new voter ID
steps.body: Once approved, your name moves to the list at your new address and is removed from the old one. You get a replacement voter ID. Return the old card.

move.sirTitle: Is your state revising its voter list?
move.sir: During a Special Intensive Revision (SIR), BLOs visit homes to check every voter. If you no longer live at your registered address, your name may be marked as shifted or absent, and it may be left off the new list. Check the draft list and apply in time.
move.toDeadlines: See SIR dates for your state

deadlines.title: Election and voter list deadlines
deadlines.lead: Know when to apply, so your name is on the list in time.
deadlines.rule: Your name must be on the voter list by the **last date of nominations** for that election. After that date the list is frozen until the election is over. An application that is still pending on that day does not count. Apply weeks early, not days.
deadlines.anytime: You can apply at any time of the year. For people turning 18, the list is updated four times a year: on 1 January, 1 April, 1 July and 1 October.
deadlines.electionsNote: ECI announces exact dates a few weeks before the polls. Until then, these dates are estimates.
deadlines.lastDateToApply: Last date to be on the list: {date}
deadlines.sirTitle: Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of voter lists
deadlines.sirLead: ECI is checking the voter list house by house in most states. If your state is listed below, check that your name is on the draft list. If it is not, file a claim during the claims and objections period.
deadlines.sirPending: Not scheduled yet: {states}. ECI will announce these later.
deadlines.sirEarlier: Earlier phases covered Bihar in 2025, and 12 states and union territories that were scheduled to finish in February 2026.
deadlines.checkCeo: Dates can change. Check your state Chief Electoral Officer (CEO) website for the latest dates.

about.title: About VotersRise
about.lead: VotersRise is a free, non-commercial guide that helps people in India get on the voter list and vote.
about.why: Every election, people find out too late that their name is missing, or they are stuck in a city far from where they are registered. The official information exists, but it is spread across many websites and is hard to follow. We put the key steps in one place, in plain language, in every scheduled language of India.
about.independent: We are not part of the Election Commission of India or any political party. We do not collect your personal data. All applications are made on official ECI websites.
about.accuracy: Every step on this site comes from official ECI forms, guidelines and press notes. Each page shows when it was last checked and lists its sources. Rules and dates change, so always confirm on the official website.
about.translation: We write every page in English. When you choose another language, the page opens through Google Translate, so its text is sent to Google for translation. Machine translation can make mistakes. If something is unclear, switch back to English or check the official website. Google Translate does not support Bodo and Kashmiri yet.
